validation.evidence: overpass-api.de (roads<300m excl. motorway/trunk/footway/steps; bicycle route relations<1km; water<500m), open-meteo elevation
geocodeFixes: kreuzweg: first hit was a farmyard near St. Georgen (in-bbox name collision), fixed via 'Kreuzweg, Kleines Wiesental' -> mountain_pass 1089m
hochblauen: first hit was Blauenstrasse in Badenweiler (425m), fixed via plain 'Hochblauen' -> peak 1156m
st-maergen: first hit was a valley bus stop at 597m, caught by elevation cross-check (expected ~890m), fixed -> village 885m
thurner: resolved via ski lift at the saddle (~1km tolerance)
titisee: lake centroid unroutable (1 road in 300m), rep point manually moved to north shore
rheindamm: linear feature, no geocode, manual rep point on the levee

anchors.name: Schauinsland
anchors.why: The classic Freiburg climb up the old Bergrennen race road with numbered hairpins to the 1284m summit and Eugen-Keidel tower.

anchors.name: Kandel
anchors.why: 1241m summit; ~970m gain in 12km from Waldkirch, gentler southern road from St. Peter over open pastures.

anchors.name: Hochblauen
anchors.why: Dead-end summit road to the 1165m Blauen with lookout tower over the Rhine plain, the signature Markgraeflerland climb.

anchors.name: Stohren
anchors.why: Brutally steep ramps near 20% from Muenstertal up to the Stohren farms, a local test piece.

anchors.name: Kreuzweg (Sirnitz)
anchors.why: Quiet 1078m crossing over the Sirnitz ridge between Muenstertal and the Kleines Wiesental, almost car-free.

anchors.name: Notschrei
anchors.why: 1121m pass linking the Schauinsland massif to the Wiesental, the standard high crossing on southern loops.

anchors.name: Wiedener Eck
anchors.why: 1036m pass with hotel at the top of the long steady Muenstertal climb, gateway to the Belchen road.

anchors.name: Thurner
anchors.why: 1036m saddle reached through the Wagensteig valley, the smoothest road link onto the high east plateau.

anchors.name: Rosskopf
anchors.why: Freiburg's gravel house climb to the 737m summit with the 1889 iron lookout tower, forest roads from several sides.

anchors.name: Kybfelsen
anchors.why: Gravel forest-road climb from Guenterstal to the granite crag looking straight down on Freiburg.

anchors.name: Totenkopf / Vogelsangpass
anchors.why: The Kaiserstuhl's 557m high point with the Neunlindenturm, paved over the Vogelsangpass, gravel to the towers.

anchors.name: Mondhalde
anchors.why: Vineyard balcony on the Kaiserstuhl west rim with the classic view across the Rhine to the Vosges.

anchors.name: Titisee
anchors.why: The Black Forest's signature lake with promenade and swim spots, classic long-loop turnaround; rep point = ST_ClosestPoint of the lake polygon to the town (centroid was open water).

anchors.name: Schluchsee
anchors.why: Largest Black Forest reservoir with rideable dam wall and shore path, the big-day extension beyond Titisee.

anchors.name: Feldsee
anchors.why: Glacial cirque lake under the Feldberg walls, reached only by gravel forest road, with the Raimartihof farm inn.

anchors.name: Windgfaellweiher
anchors.why: Quiet forest swim lake with a small lido just off the Baehnle-Radweg, calmer than Titisee.

anchors.name: Opfinger See
anchors.why: Freiburg's gravel-pit swim lake in the Mooswald, the standard hot-day after-work ride.

anchors.name: Tunisee
anchors.why: Swim lake with campsite and beach bar on the flat Rhine-plain approach north of Freiburg.

anchors.name: Schlossberg
anchors.why: Lookout tower and Kanonenplatz terrace directly above the old town; mostly useful for very short loops.

anchors.name: Kaiserstuhl loess tracks
anchors.why: Dense network of sunken loess lanes (Hohlwege) and vineyard tracks over volcanic terraces, the region's premier gravel terrain. Rep point: Bickensohl.

anchors.name: Tuniberg vineyard lanes
anchors.why: Compact ridge of vineyard service roads with Kaiserstuhl and Vosges views, the closest vineyard playground to the city.

anchors.name: Mooswald
anchors.why: Grid of flat hard-packed forest roads, the fast tempo terrain and traffic-free corridor toward Tuniberg and the Rhine.

anchors.name: Rhine dam Breisach-Burkheim
anchors.why: Dead-flat gravel levee along the Restrhein for kilometers, the go-to long steady gravel corridor on the French border.

anchors.name: Staufen im Breisgau
anchors.why: Faust legend town with castle ruin in the vineyards, the classic coffee stop before or after Muenstertal climbs.

anchors.name: St. Peter
anchors.why: Baroque abbey with twin onion towers at 720m, the crossroads of nearly every Kandel and plateau loop.

anchors.name: St. Maergen
anchors.why: Monastery village at ~890m on the famous panorama road from St. Peter, lined with Black Forest farms.

anchors.name: Breisach
anchors.why: Muenster hill town rising out of the Rhine plain, the standard western turnaround with the bridge to France.

anchors.name: Burkheim
anchors.why: Medieval one-street wine village with the Schwendi castle ruin, the prettiest stop on a Kaiserstuhl circuit.

anchors.name: Endingen
anchors.why: Old town square with gabled Kornhaus at the Kaiserstuhl's north foot, natural entry of northern vineyard loops.

anchors.name: Glottertal
anchors.why: Wine-and-farm valley of Schwarzwaldklinik fame, the scenic low-traffic approach to Kandel and St. Peter.

anchors.name: Muenstertal (St. Trudpert)
anchors.why: Stretched valley village around St. Trudpert abbey, launch pad for Stohren, Wiedener Eck, Kreuzweg and Sirnitz.

anchors.name: Sulzburg
anchors.why: Former silver-mining town with one of Germany's oldest churches (St. Cyriak), tucked into a quiet climbing valley.

anchors.name: Ihringen
anchors.why: Reputedly Germany's warmest village, gateway to the Winklerberg terraces and southern Kaiserstuhl ramps.

anchors.name: Badenweiler
anchors.why: Spa town with Roman bath ruins at the foot of the Hochblauen climb.

anchors.name: Hirschsprung (Hoellental)
anchors.why: The stag monument in the Hoellental gorge; survives validation because the parallel bike path and old road are routable (B31 itself is not).

anchors.name: Simonswaelder Tal
anchors.why: Quiet wooded valley ending in the steep Guetenbach wall climb, a low-traffic way deeper into the Black Forest.

anchors.name: Nonnenmattweiher
anchors.why: Remote moor cirque lake with a floating peat island, reached by gravel high in the southern Black Forest.

anchors.name: Katharinenkapelle
anchors.why: Chapel knoll on the northern Kaiserstuhl rim with a wide view over Endingen and the Rhine plain.

anchors.name: Eichelspitzturm
anchors.why: Modern steel tower on the 521m Eichelspitze on the Kaiserstuhl ridge gravel route.

anchors.name: Maria Lindenberg
anchors.why: Pilgrimage chapel knoll above St. Peter with a postcard view of the abbey against the Kandel.

anchors.name: Schoenberg / Schneeburg
anchors.why: Castle ruin on Freiburg's house hill, vineyard and forest gravel between Ebringen and Wittnau.

anchors.name: Waldkirch
anchors.why: Organ-builder town below the Kastelburg ruin, base of the Kandel's hardest paved side.

anchors.name: Elztal
anchors.why: Gentle valley corridor with continuous bike path along the Elz toward Elzach and the central Black Forest. Rep point: Bleibach.

anchors.name: Hexental
anchors.why: Freiburg's after-work training valley below the Schoenberg, feeding the Geiersnest and St. Ulrich climbs. Rep point: Soelden.
